title: Fleet surge detection and emergency scaling escape hatch
creator: Marin Chen
description: Summary: During a customer-facing peak on 2025-02-10 we observed a rapid capacity shortfall in multiple Dedicated pools that caused sustained latency SLO misses for several high-commit customers. The incident stemmed from an unintended interaction between a new autoscaler change and delayed telemetry ingestion from the fleet controller. This ticket captures the emergency steps taken, the temporary escape hatch implemented to protect SLAs, the full timeline, root cause analysis, and a prioritized set of postmortem action items for preventing recurrence.
timeline: 2025-02-10 03:10 UTC - Alerts: multiple Dedicated pool latency alerts escalated (p95 token latency > 2x target) and queue depth increased in region us-west2.
2025-02-10 03:14 UTC - Triage: on-call engaged. Initial hypothesis: burst traffic. We observed autoscaler did not provision new nodes for ~8 minutes.
2025-02-10 03:22 UTC - Mitigation: emergency manual scale executed for affected pools; routing rules updated to shift low-tier customers to burst spare capacity.

2025-02-10 03:40 UTC - Temporary escape hatch: enabled 'degraded-routing' policy which (a) relaxed strict per-customer concurrency caps for enterprise tiers and (b) immediately pinned critical workloads to hot-reserve nodes.
2025-02-10 04:05 UTC - Stabilized: latency returned to within SLOs for pinned customers. Broader pool throughput normalized after autoscaler corrections were rolled back.
2025-02-11 through 2025-02-28 - Investigation period: logs/metrics sweep, ingestion pipeline replay, and autoscaler config audit.
2025-03-03 - Draft action items and mitigation proposals reviewed with SRE, Runtime, and Product.
2025-03-04 - This ticket updated with final RCA summary and prioritized remediation backlog.
steps_taken: Executed manual node provisioning for 6 affected dedicated pools to provide immediate headroom.
Temporarily increased per-customer concurrency caps for enterprise plans via routing policy to avoid queuing on customer-facing routes.
Rolled back the autoscaler change (config v2025-02-09) that introduced delayed reconciliation in the presence of partial telemetry windows.
Restarted fleet controller ingestion job and replayed 45 minutes of queued telemetry to reconstruct state.
Implemented short-term alert suppression for noisy internal metrics while preserving customer-facing SLO alerts.
root_cause: A recent autoscaler improvement intended to reduce churn introduced a grace window that postponed scale-out decisions when telemetry arrival rate dropped below a threshold. During a legitimate traffic spike combined with transient telemetry ingestion lag from an internal Kafka partition, the autoscaler deferred provisioning for ~8 minutes. The fleet controller also failed to expose the pending scale decision to routing, so requests queued instead of being shifted to hot-reserve nodes.
observability_gaps: No single dashboard correlating telemetry ingestion health (Kafka lag) with autoscaler decision latency and per-pool queue depth.
Missing synthetic checks for the autoscaler reconciliation loop under partial telemetry conditions.
Alert thresholds were tied to raw queue depth without a short-window derivative to detect sudden growth rates.
action_items: ENG-37820: Ship autoscaler config guardrail that rejects grace-window values > 30s unless approved by SRE (owner: Diego Alvarez, due: 2025-03-12)
ENG-37821: Build cross-team dashboard that joins Kafka consumer lag, autoscaler last-decision timestamp, and per-pool QPS/queue-size (owner: Priya Nair, due: 2025-03-17)
ENG-37822: Add a synthetic canary that simulates partial telemetry and validates autoscaler responds within 90s (owner: Alex Romero, due: 2025-03-24)
ENG-37823: Implement an escape-hatch API to force immediate routing to hot-reserve nodes per-customer and document playbook (owner: SRE On-call, due: 2025-03-10)
ENG-37824: Modify alerting to include both absolute queue depth and a short-window growth-rate alert to catch rapid surges (owner: Marisol Vega, due: 2025-03-14)
ENG-37825: Run a tabletop incident drill covering telemetry lag + autoscaler regression scenarios in Cycle 43 (owner: Oncall Rotation Lead, due: 2025-04-01)
postmortem_notes: We treated this event as a near-miss for customers on enterprise plans who were pinned successfully by the escape hatch; however, several mid-tier customers experienced degraded latency for ~18 minutes.
Communication: Customer success issued notifications to impacted accounts within 4 hours; we committed to a root-cause update in 7 days and a follow-up meeting for top customers.

Risk: The root cause shows a class of failures where control-plane ingestion delays can silently affect autoscaler behavior. This requires instrumentation and guardrails rather than pure reliance on rollout testing.
notes_for_release: Include autoscaler guardrails and observability dashboard in runtime-1.20 release notes under 'Resilience and autoscaler improvements'. Clearly document escape-hatch usage and permissioning.
communication_plan: Prepare a short incident summary for public status page (owner: Product Ops, target: 2025-03-06)
Schedule 1:1s with top 10 impacted customers to review mitigation and roadmap (owner: CS Lead, target: 2025-03-14)
Post an internal RFC describing safe autoscaler parameter ranges and approval flow (owner: Runtime PM, target: 2025-03-12)
